ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` (Anointed.cs:15-18) == cost 1 / SKILL / RARE / SELF. No CanonicalVars on either side (the count is computed, not printed).

OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `cards.pool.take_random` is `IEnumerableExtensions.TakeRandom` (IEnumerableExtensions.cs:17-20) -- `collection.ToList().UnstableShuffle(rng).Take(count)` -- and it encodes all three things `random.sample` got wrong: a FULL Fisher-Yates whatever `count` is (so the stream lands where the game's does), over a COPY (`.ToList()`), with no clamp on `count` (`Take(n)` on a shorter sequence yields the whole thing). Anointed.cs:23 routes to `combat_rng.card_selection`, the stream it names. THE INPUT ORDER IS PART OF THE FIX: `PileType.Draw.GetPile(Owner).Cards` is TOP-FIRST and the sim stores the top at the END of `draw_pile`, and UnstableShuffle's output depends on the input order and not just on the membership, so the candidate list is built from `reversed(player.draw_pile)`. The count stays `MAX_HAND_SIZE - len(hand)` with no `min`, because `Take` needs none.  Pinned by test/test_take_random_streams.py, which gives every named accessor its own Random and asserts the site advanced the one its C# names and did NOT touch the shared `combat._rng`.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: WRONG RNG STREAM AND WRONG SELECTION ALGORITHM. C#: `PileType.Draw.GetPile(Owner).Cards.Where(c => c.Rarity == Rare).TakeRandom(count, Owner.RunState.Rng.CombatCardSelection)` (Anointed.cs:23), and `TakeRandom` is `collection.ToList().UnstableShuffle(rng).Take(count)` (IEnumerableExtensions.cs:17-20) -- a full Fisher-Yates over the candidate list on the named CombatCardSelection stream, then take-first-N. The sim calls `ctx.combat._rng.sample(rares, min(space, len(rares)))` (colorless_skills.py:82): the unseeded shared `random.Random`, not `ctx.combat.combat_rng.card_selection` (the accessor exists -- combat_rng.py:21,55 maps `card_selection -> combat_card_selection`), and `random.sample` is a reservoir/partial-selection algorithm, not shuffle-then-take, so even fed the same stream it would consume a different number of draws in a different order. Observable: under a string-seeded parity/conformance run the set of Rare cards pulled into hand differs from the recorded run, and the CombatCardSelection stream desyncs for everything downstream. The count itself is faithful (`CardPile.MaxCardsInHand` is 10, CardPile.cs:21, == `player.MAX_HAND_SIZE = 10`, player.py:56). LIVE -- Anointed is a ported Rare colorless Skill reachable from the colorless pool, and the parity streams it should be using are already wired (`CombatRng.parity`, combat_rng.py:41-46). REGRESSION TEST: `test/test_rng_tripwire.py:33` (`test_no_wrong_stream_draws_in_random_run`, 20 seeded full runs) is the standing gate for this whole family. It wraps `RunState.rng` and asserts ZERO in-combat draws on it; `CombatState` receives that same object as `self._rng` (run.py:1146-1148, combat.py:88), so a `ctx.combat._rng` draw taken from inside a card's `on_play` is recorded and fails the gate -- verified by playing this family's shape under a `Tripwire` and getting a hit at the `card.on_play` frame (combat.py:490). The gate is green today, so these 20 seeds never reach this card's draw; routing the site to the named `combat_rng` accessor is verified by keeping it green.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `AddKeyword(CardKeyword.Retain)` (Anointed.cs:29) == `self.retain = True`, and unlike aggression/apparition this card DOES re-seed the flag in `_init_vars` (`self.retain = False`, colorless_skills.py:73), so `downgrade()` restores it -- confirmed by `py audit/tools/card_probes.py downgrade`, which does not list anointed.

guards.what: count = MaxCardsInHand - Hand.Count can be <= 0 when the hand is already full (Anointed.cs:22)
guards.rationale: C# `Take(count)` with count <= 0 yields nothing; the sim's `min(space, len(rares))` with `space <= 0` makes `random.sample(..., <=0)` return `[]` (a negative would raise, but `space` is `10 - len(hand)` and the hand is capped at 10 by player.py:278, so it cannot go negative). Same outcome.

guards.what: cards are moved to the hand with CardPileCmd.Add(cards, PileType.Hand) (Anointed.cs:24) vs direct list mutation
guards.issue: The sim pops each card out of `player.draw_pile` and appends to `player.hand` in place (colorless_skills.py:83-84) instead of routing through a pile-add verb, so nothing fires for the pile transition. C# `CardPileCmd.Add` runs `Hook.AfterCardChangedPiles` (CardPileCmd.cs:635) and enforces `MaxCardsInHand` inside `AddInternal`. This is the card-level instance of creature_card_cmds's 'no unified AfterCardChangedPiles' structural finding (docs/audit/seams/creature_card_cmds.md:643-666), recorded here because it is Anointed's own code doing the bypass, not the machinery's. Note these cards arrive in hand WITHOUT being 'drawn', so no on_card_drawn is expected on either side. DORMANT: the sim has no `after_card_changed_piles` listener at all, so nothing observable is dropped until such a listener is ported; the concrete unported thing that makes it live is any C# model overriding `AfterCardChangedPiles` for a Draw->Hand move.
